summary.text: Don Leonard is the Democratic nominee for Ohio's 15th Congressional District. He is a professor of city and regional planning at The Ohio State University and a former U.S. Peace Corps volunteer, and he won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary over Adam Miller. In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey he describes his campaign as centered on household costs for working families.

paragraphs.text: In his Ballotpedia survey, describes growing up as the son of a single mother and says his childhood included periods when poverty and homelessness were close.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science (2001) and a master's degree in regional development (2003) from the University of Massachusetts, Lowell.
Served two years in the U.S. Peace Corps in South America after college, according to his survey.
Earned a Ph.D. in government from Cornell University (2013).
Works as a professor of city and regional planning at The Ohio State University.
Defeated Adam Miller in the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary, 52.9% to 47.1%.
Says he and his wife had a daughter in January 2025 and that the birth was part of his decision to run for office.
